subject: Mathematics
name: Specialist Mathematics, Units 1 and 2
about: VCE, Proof, vectors, complex numbers and discrete maths
syllabus: VCE Mathematics Study Design (from 2023), Specialist Mathematics Units 1 and 2

units.title: Unit 1: Proof, logic, graphs, sequences and combinatorics

points.title: Number systems and sets
points.brief: The natural numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers, and set notation such as union, intersection, complement and subset.

points.title: Primes and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic
points.brief: Every whole number above 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way, and there are infinitely many primes.

points.title: Quantifiers
points.brief: For all and there exists say how widely a statement applies. A single counterexample disproves a for all statement.

points.title: Direct proof
points.brief: Start from what is known and reason step by step to the result, such as proving the sum of two even numbers is even.

points.title: Examples and counterexamples
points.brief: Examples can support a claim but never prove it for all cases. One counterexample is enough to disprove it.

points.title: Proof by contrapositive
points.brief: To prove if P then Q, prove if not Q then not P instead.

points.title: Proof by contradiction
points.brief: Assume the result is false and show this leads to something impossible, as in proving √2 is irrational.

points.title: Mathematical induction
points.brief: Show a statement holds for the first case, and that holding for n means it holds for n + 1. Then it holds for all.

points.title: Proofs about numbers
points.brief: Simple proofs about divisibility, sequences and series, inequalities and irrational numbers such as the square root of 2.

points.title: Statements and connectives
points.brief: Propositions joined by and, or and not, with truth tables and Karnaugh maps showing when a compound statement is true.

points.title: Conditional statements
points.brief: The statement if P then Q is false only when P is true and Q is false. Its contrapositive, if not Q then not P, means the same.

points.title: Converse and equivalence
points.brief: The converse of if P then Q is if Q then P, which is not always true. When both hold, P and Q are equivalent.

points.title: Boolean algebra
points.brief: The laws of Boolean algebra simplify statements and sets, and show which arguments are valid and which are tautologies.

points.title: Logic gates and circuits
points.brief: AND, OR and NOT gates build circuits that follow Boolean rules, and simplifying the logic simplifies the circuit.

points.title: Binary numbers
points.brief: Numbers written in base 2 with only 0s and 1s, as computers store them, and converting to and from base 10.

points.title: Algorithms and pseudocode
points.brief: An algorithm uses sequence, decisions (if-then) and repetition (loops), written in pseudocode.

points.title: Graph theory in Specialist
points.brief: Graphs of vertices and edges model molecules, circuits and networks. The degrees of all vertices add to twice the number of edges.

points.title: Types of graphs
points.brief: Simple, complete, bipartite and regular graphs, subgraphs, complements, and isomorphic graphs that are the same in structure.

points.title: Planar graphs and Euler's formula
points.brief: A planar graph can be drawn with no edges crossing. For a connected one, vertices minus edges plus faces equals 2.

points.title: Trees
points.brief: A tree is connected with no cycles, and a tree with n vertices always has n - 1 edges.

points.title: Euler and Hamilton
points.brief: An Euler trail uses each edge once, as in the Königsberg bridge problem; a Hamiltonian path visits each vertex once.

points.title: Matrix operations in Specialist
points.brief: Matrix notation and order, using matrices to hold data, and adding, scaling and multiplying them.

points.title: Determinants and matrix equations
points.brief: The determinant shows whether a square matrix has an inverse, which solves matrix equations such as AX = B.

points.title: Arithmetic and geometric series
points.brief: An arithmetic series sums to n/2 × (2a + (n − 1)d). A geometric series sums to a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1).

points.title: Infinite geometric series
points.brief: When −1 < r < 1, a geometric series sums to a/(1 − r).

points.title: Recurrence relations in Specialist
points.brief: Sequences defined from earlier terms, including second-order ones such as the Fibonacci sequence.

points.title: The pigeonhole principle
points.brief: If more than n items go into n boxes, some box holds at least two.

points.title: The inclusion-exclusion principle
points.brief: To count A or B, add the counts of A and B, then subtract those in both.

points.title: Permutations and combinations
points.brief: Counting arrangements and selections, with or without repeated items, and with conditions such as two people sitting together.

points.title: Combinatorial identities
points.brief: Results such as nCr = nC(n - r), proved by counting the same thing in two ways.

units.title: Unit 2: Sampling, trigonometry, vectors, complex numbers and curves

points.title: Sums of random variables
points.brief: Adding two independent copies of a discrete random variable gives a different distribution from doubling one copy.

points.title: Simulation
points.brief: Using random numbers to model a chance process many times and estimate a probability.

points.title: Sample means vary
points.brief: The mean of a sample changes from one sample to the next. Larger samples vary less.

points.title: Distributions of sample means
points.brief: Plotting the means of many samples shows their spread, which narrows as sample size grows.

points.title: Radians, arcs and segments
points.brief: Radian measure, arc length, and the areas of sectors and segments of a circle.

points.title: Sine and cosine rules in three dimensions
points.brief: The sine and cosine rules solve triangles in solid shapes, such as the angle between two planes.

points.title: Compound and double angle formulas
points.brief: Formulas such as sin(A + B) and cos 2A rewrite trigonometric expressions, prove identities and give exact values.

points.title: Matrices as transformations
points.brief: A 2 × 2 matrix maps points in the plane, giving dilations, reflections, rotations and shears.

points.title: Composition and inverse transformations
points.brief: Doing one transformation then another multiplies their matrices. The inverse matrix undoes a transformation.

points.title: Determinants and area
points.brief: The determinant of a transformation matrix scales areas, and some properties stay the same under a transformation.

points.title: Vectors in the plane
points.brief: A vector has size and direction, written as a column or with i and j components.

points.title: Adding and scaling vectors
points.brief: Vectors add head to tail. Multiplying by a scalar stretches or reverses them.

points.title: Magnitude and unit vectors
points.brief: The magnitude of ai + bj is √(a² + b²). A unit vector has magnitude 1.

points.title: The scalar product
points.brief: a·b = |a||b|cos θ. Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular when their scalar product is zero.

points.title: Vector projections
points.brief: The projection of a onto b gives the part of a in the direction of b.

points.title: Proof with vectors
points.brief: Vectors can prove geometric results, such as that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

points.title: Vectors in motion
points.brief: Vectors model displacement, velocity, relative velocity, forces in balance and motion under a constant force.

points.title: The imaginary unit
points.brief: i is defined by i² = −1, so square roots of negative numbers can be written, such as √−9 = 3i.

points.title: Arithmetic with complex numbers
points.brief: Complex numbers a + bi add, subtract and multiply like binomials, using i² = −1.

points.title: Conjugates and division
points.brief: The conjugate of a + bi is a − bi. Dividing uses the conjugate to make the denominator real.

points.title: The Argand plane
points.brief: A complex number is plotted with its real part on the horizontal axis and imaginary part on the vertical.

chapters.title: Polar form and the complex plane

points.title: Modulus and argument
points.brief: The modulus is the distance from the origin; the argument is the angle from the positive real axis.

points.title: Polar form
points.brief: A complex number written as r cis θ. Multiplying multiplies the moduli and adds the arguments.

points.title: Solving quadratics over the complex numbers
points.brief: A quadratic with a negative discriminant has two complex roots that are conjugates.

points.title: Regions in the complex plane
points.brief: Equations and inequalities in z describe lines, rays, circles, ellipses and regions on the Argand plane.

points.title: Partial fractions
points.brief: Splitting a rational function into simpler fractions with linear or quadratic denominators, by equating coefficients.

points.title: Reciprocal functions
points.brief: Graphs of y = 1/f(x), including the reciprocal circular functions sec, cosec and cot, with asymptotes where f(x) = 0.

points.title: Inverse circular functions
points.brief: arcsin, arccos and arctan undo sin, cos and tan on restricted domains, each with its own graph.

points.title: The absolute value function
points.brief: y = |x| makes every output non-negative, giving a V-shaped graph that can be transformed.

points.title: Circles and ellipses
points.brief: Lines, circles and ellipses defined as loci of points, with their Cartesian, polar and parametric forms.

points.title: Parabolas and hyperbolas
points.brief: Parabolas and hyperbolas as loci, their equations and graphs, including the asymptotes of a hyperbola.

points.title: Parametric equations
points.brief: x and y are each given in terms of a parameter t, which can trace curves such as circles.

points.title: Polar coordinates
points.brief: A point is given by its distance r from the origin and angle θ, with x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ.
